papers.title: Geometry-aware similarity metrics for neural representations on Riemannian and statistical manifolds
papers.abstract: Similarity measures such as centred kernel alignment (CKA) or representational similarity analysis (RSA) are widely used to compare the representational geometries employed by different neural networks to solve the same task. Yet, because existing methods compare the extrinsic geometry of representations in state space, rather than their intrinsic geometry, they may fail to capture subtle yet crucial distinctions between fundamentally different computations. Here, we introduce metric similarity analysis (MSA), a novel method which leverages tools from Riemannian geometry to compare the intrinsic geometry of neural representations under the manifold hypothesis. We show that MSA can be used to (i) disentangle neural computations of deep networks in rich vs. lazy learning regimes, (ii) compare the dynamics of recurrent neural networks and state-space models, and (iii) investigate the statistical manifolds of diffusion models. Overall, we introduce a mathematically grounded and broadly applicable framework to understand the mechanisms behind neural computations by contrasting their intrinsic geometries.

papers.title: The Fast Tree Transform
papers.abstract: The Fast Tree Transform is a locally-aggregated transform defined for arbitrary graph geometries that generalizes both the Hadamard frequency transform and the Haar wavelet transform on the circle. The pure frequency part of the transform approximately diagonalizes the graph Laplacian; this fact makes it useful as a preconditioner in geometric optimization problems. The full transform provides an only slightly-redundant representation of signals on the graph that allows sparse representation of signals that include both edges and textures.

papers.title: Convergence of finite element exterior calculus for the Hodge-Dirac and Hodge-Laplace problems on closed Riemannian manifolds
papers.abstract: We prove that the finite element exterior calculus (FEEC) approximation to the Hodge-Dirac and Hodge-Laplace problems on any closed oriented Riemannian manifold converges. Its approximate solutions, together with their exterior derivatives, converge to the continuum solutions for every source, and at the rate of the mesh size when the source and its codifferential are square integrable. We use Licht's estimate for the FEEC approximation of forms with one square-integrable derivative by finite element forms. We combine this with a new abstract error bound for approximations of Hilbert complexes. This bound uses a version of Di Pietro and Droniou's third Strang lemma. To apply these estimates, we show that every closed manifold admits a family of arbitrarily fine triangulations whose shapes stay uniformly under control.

papers.title: Special Lagrangian cones in Deep Learning
papers.abstract: We introduce a matrix generalization of the cone of Harvey and Lawson and prove that it is an exact special Lagrangian manifold. We further show that it belongs to a family of exact special Lagrangian manifolds that foliate the balanced manifold arising in deep learning.

papers.title: On deformations of foliated complex analytic structures IV-1: Obstructed and unobstructed foliated deformations
papers.abstract: We study obstructions of deformations of foliated complex analytic structures. We describe obstructions in terms of Cech resolutions. From foliated complex analytic families in Part I and unfolded complex analytic families in Part III, we deduce the integrability conditions. We identify infinitesimal deformations and obstructions in terms of Dolbeault resolutions or Dolbeault type bicomplexes from the integrability conditions. Then we describe the correspondences of infinitesimal deformations and obstructions between Cech resolutions, and Dolbeault resolutions or Dolbeault type bicomplexes.

papers.title: The Whitney Extension Problem in Carnot groups
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbb{G}$ be a Carnot group, let $E \subset \mathbb{G}$ be compact, and suppose we are given a function $f: E \to \mathbb{R}$. The $C^1_H$ {\em Whitney Extension Problem} asks the following: what must be true about $f$ to guarantee that there exists a smooth, horizontal function $F \in C^1_H(\mathbb{G})$ extending $f$, i.e., there is some $F:\mathbb{G} \to \mathbb{R}$ such that $F|_E = f|_E$ and $XF$ is continuous for every horizontal left invariant vector field $X$? We adapt the method of G. Glaeser and C. Fefferman to answer this question in this non-commutative setting. Moreover, we provide an alternative solution to the $C^1$ Whitney Extension Problem for horizontal curves in the Heisenberg group.

papers.title: Local regularity and p-harmonic approximation for weak inverse mean curvature flow
papers.abstract: We prove local Lipschitz regularity for locally bounded $BV$ solutions of the calibration equations for inverse mean curvature flow. We also approximate every prescribed variational weak flow locally by Moser's logarithmic transforms of positive $p$-harmonic functions. On a fixed smooth domain, with the trace of a calibrated Lipschitz solution prescribed, both the uniform error and the absolute difference of total variations are $O((p-1)^{1/3})$ as $p\downarrow1$. In particular, the approximations converge strictly in $BV$.

papers.title: Classification of 3-dimensional complex nilmanifolds - Teichm\"uller and moduli spaces
papers.abstract: We classify complex nilmanifolds of dimension three by describing the Teichm\"uller and moduli spaces of left-invariant complex structures for every real six-dimensional nilmanifold.

papers.title: Lie-Lions brackets of nonlocal vector fields
papers.abstract: We study nonlocal vector fields on the space of probability measures with finite second moment. Using Lions derivatives, we define their Lie-Lions bracket, which adds to the spatial Lie bracket a correction due to the evolution of the law, and prove that its vanishing is equivalent to commutation of the global flows, under first-order regularity and linear growth assumptions. We then construct a Lie algebra of complete polynomial nonlocal fields. For this class, we establish commutator and second-order Baker-Campbell-Hausdorff formulas with cubic remainders in the Wasserstein distance $W_2$, controlled by the second moment and uniform in the number of particles. The proofs rely on finite-particle realizations, which preserve the bracket and jointly determine the nonlocal field. We also obtain uniform estimates for smooth bounded kernels and a Leibniz rule for the action of polynomial fields on polynomial observables. Examples from collective dynamics show that the vanishing of the spatial bracket at a fixed law is neither necessary nor sufficient for commutation. They concern symmetries, aggregation-dependent rotation, synchronization, the transmission of a turn along a hierarchy, effective three-body interactions and occupancy-dependent circulation.

papers.title: Microlocal properties of Cauchy evolution under metric variations
papers.abstract: We develop the microlocal analysis of the Cauchy evolution for wave-type equations on the infinite-dimensional space of Lorentzian metrics. We regard the Cauchy evolution operator as a distributional function of the metric, and give this notion a precise meaning through restrictions to finite-dimensional families of metrics. We study the singularities of this metric dependence. For normally hyperbolic operators on vector bundles, we determine the resulting operator-valued wavefront sets. Their parameter covectors are given by integrals of metric variations along individual null geodesics. At ultrastatic ends, metric dependence also determines the time-translation generators and their positive- and negative-energy splitting. More generally, the parameter singularities distinguish the two characteristic sheets and can be used to reconstruct the ordinary Cauchy propagation relation, which describes propagation of singularities. Consequences include smoothing under parameter averaging and polar-cone bounds associated with averaged null-positive variations, linking the result to averaged null energy conditions. The analysis also covers the Cauchy evolution of the Dirac equation.

papers.title: Strong unique continuation on Riemannian manifolds for degenerate elliptic operators with convexified weights
papers.abstract: In this manuscript, we consider a degenerate elliptic equation on a Riemannian manifold whose weight vanishes at an interior point $p$, and prove the strong unique continuation property (SUCP) at $p$. The curved setting gives rise to intrinsic geometric error terms that obstruct the analytic estimates available in the Euclidean case. To overcome this, we introduce a convexified radial weight that restores coercivity in the Carleman commutator. Combining the resulting Carleman estimate with a Hardy-type inequality and a Caccioppoli inequality, we show that any weak solution vanishing to infinite order at the degeneracy point must be identically zero on the connected domain. This result is the first SUCP theorem for this class of degenerate operators on general Riemannian manifolds.

papers.title: On the index of two-dimensional elliptic end-periodic operators
papers.abstract: This paper investigates the index problem for elliptic end-periodic differential operators on a two-dimensional manifold with a cylindrical end. We define the topological index as the sum of the contribution of the interior symbol, expressed by an Atiyah--Singer type integral, and the contribution of the limit operator, expressed in terms of the Melrose type eta-invariant and a correction term that depends on the lower order terms of the limit operator. We prove the homotopy invariance of the topological index, which allows us to reduce the original problem to the study of operators of a simpler form by employing $K$-theoretic methods.

papers.title: Smooth local isometric embeddings in dimension four
papers.abstract: We prove that every smooth four-dimensional Riemannian metric admits, near each point, a local isometric embedding into $\mathbb{R}^{10}$, and that this universal dimension is optimal. A Gram criterion constructs a regular analytic embedding of the Euclidean metric from a rational positive semidefinite tensor obtained by signed evaluations. A specified finite-field minor certifies characteristic regularity. The real-principal-type construction of Nakamura and Maeda gives openness of the metric map on a fixed ball. Rescaling then applies it to arbitrary smooth metrics.

papers.title: A second-order estimate linear in the gradient for complex Hessian equations
papers.abstract: We use the maximum principle to prove a second-order estimate with linear dependence on the gradient for the nondegenerate complex Hessian equation on a compact K\"ahler manifold. The proof combines $C^0$ compactness and a refined concavity inequality with the use of nearby smooth admissible functions. A standard interpolation argument then yields the known uniform gradient and complex Hessian bounds.

papers.title: Bott--Chern and Aeppli Cohomology of toroidal groups
papers.abstract: We compute the Bott--Chern and Aeppli cohomology groups of theta toroidal groups in arbitrary dimensions, obtaining explicit dimension formulas and bases in all bidegrees. For general toroidal groups, we determine the Hausdorff reductions of these cohomology groups and show that they coincide with those of theta toroidal groups. We also compute the Bott--Chern and Aeppli cohomology groups themselves in certain specific bidegrees, without passing to their Hausdorff reductions.

papers.title: Global Classification of the Flat Singular Escobar-Yamabe Equation
papers.abstract: In every dimension $n\geq3$, we classify positive solutions of the flat Escobar--Yamabe equation on the Euclidean half-space with a possible isolated boundary singularity at the origin. Solutions with a removable singularity are boundary bubbles. Up to dilation, the nonremovable solutions are the cylindrical solution and a family of periodic Delaunay solutions uniquely parametrized by the necksize $\epsilon \in (0,1)$, the minimum of the normalized boundary trace. In each fundamental period $T_\epsilon$, the trace has exactly two critical points, a nondegenerate minimum and a nondegenerate maximum. The period and the solution centered at the trace minimum and rescaled to period one depend smoothly on $\epsilon$. As $\epsilon \to 0$, $T_\epsilon = \frac{4}{n-2}\log(1/\epsilon)+O(1)$. As $\epsilon \to 1$, the solutions converge to the cylindrical solution and their periods tend to that of its linearized oscillation. We use uniqueness in the odd and even classes for linear Robin equations to obtain reflection symmetry and continuation in the necksize.

papers.title: Geometric Endpoints, Global Trajectories, and Teichm\"uller Projection for the M\"obius-Invariant Willmore Flow
papers.abstract: We study endpoints and conformal projection of the M\"obius-invariant Willmore flow in the round three-sphere. Under uniform nonumbilicity or an integrable weighted condition, image-measure transport yields a unique finite-time integral-varifold limit. Reduced Hopf trajectories have unique anchored finite-time profile and marked conformal endpoints at arbitrary energy. Every smooth global reduced trajectory converges smoothly modulo reparametrization to an elastic profile, with quantitative rates and finite dissipation length. We compute the differential of the conformal-class projection along reduced trajectories and prove that its maximal rank persists at every finite time when it holds initially. Near the Clifford torus, Hopf tori with the same marked conformal type can have noncollinear projected velocities, ruling out a common autonomous Teichm\"uller equation even after positive time recalibrations.

papers.title: The topology of end-periodic smoothing operators
papers.abstract: We develop an algebra of smoothing operators adapted to the geometry of end-periodic manifolds. We extend the renormalized trace and trace defect formula of Mrowka-Ruberman-Saveliev to this algebra, and establish a Fredholm criterion and winding-number index formula for smoothing perturbations of the identity. Our main result computes the homotopy groups of the associated end-periodic smoothing group. This provides a foundation for future work on relative index theory for families of end-periodic differential operators.

papers.title: On evolution of mean curvature and minimal areas in general codimension for inverse problems
papers.abstract: Many seemingly standard formulas for the evolution of the mean curvature vector in higher codimension assume only normal variations, which are ill-suited for analyzing the evolution of submanifolds- with-boundary whose boundaries may not be moving orthogonally at each time. Such situations arise when one considers inverse problems for minimal areas, for example, where such boundaries are confined to a larger ambient boundary. In this note, we provide coordinate-free identities for use in such problems, including higher order derivatives of mean curvature. We translate these identities to some of the existing inverse problem literature in codimension one. We also hope readers may find the computational framework helpful in other situations arising in geometric analysis.

papers.title: Branch Obstructions for Area-Minimizing Currents and Flat Critical Points of Weakly-Conformal Maps
papers.abstract: We study two problems motivated by the local geometry of conformal $\phi$-curves. First, let $T$ be a $k$-dimensional locally area-minimizing integral current in Euclidean space, with $k\geq3$, codimension at least two, no boundary, and a locally conformally flat induced metric on $\operatorname{reg} T$. We prove the following branch obstruction: at any rapid-decay branch point whose planar frequency differs from $2$, every nonzero cyclic component of every cylindrical normalized tangent function has repetition multiplicity at least two. Consequently, the nonintegral-frequency points of densities $2$ and $3$ in the rapid-decay branch set have Hausdorff dimension at most $k-3$. On the full branch set, they have zero $\mathcal H^{k-2}$ measure. These conclusions apply to Euclidean image currents of conformal $\phi$-curves with locally conformally flat domains, provided the image currents satisfy the stated hypotheses. Second, for $C^j$ weakly-conformal maps between smooth Riemannian manifolds, with domain dimension $k\geq3$ and $j\geq2$, we prove that all derivatives of orders $1$ through $j$ vanish at every critical point. As a consequence, for smooth weakly-conformal maps with connected domain, we establish a curvature condition under which the map is constant or has no critical points. The flatness and continuation results apply in particular to conformal $\phi$-curves with the corresponding regularity and curvature assumptions. Finally, we examine the Bor\r{u}vka cone, which illustrates the role of regularity and the distinction between critical points and branch points.

papers.title: Non-connected minimal clusters of small volume in a compact Finsler manifold
papers.abstract: We prove that isoperimetric clusters in general Finsler manifolds can be disconnected even when the volume constraint is small. This is in contrast with the Riemannian case and the ``fixed-norm'' case, where connectedness for arbitrarily small volume has recently been proved.

papers.title: The Cheng--Yau gradient estimate for Jacobi fields
papers.abstract: We prove a pointwise gradient estimate for positive Jacobi fields on minimal hypersurfaces of dimension two and three, inspired by the Cheng--Yau estimate for harmonic functions. The estimate also controls the second fundamental form, and so provides yet another proof of the stable Bernstein theorem in dimensions two and three.

papers.title: Delaunay Asymptotics for the Singular Escobar-Yamabe Equation
papers.abstract: In dimensions $n\geq3$, we prove that near an isolated boundary singularity a positive solution of the Escobar--Yamabe equation for a smooth metric approaches a fixed periodic Delaunay solution or the cylindrical solution if its trace lies between positive multiples of $|\overline x|^{-(n-2)/2}$, where $\overline x$ is the tangential Fermi coordinate. The relative error decays at a positive power rate, with weighted estimates through two derivatives in Fermi coordinates. The necksize is unique, and the translation parameter is unique modulo the least positive period in the periodic case. The Hamiltonian smoothly parametrizes the periodic family modulo translation. We classify Jacobi fields of polynomial growth at both ends without assuming symmetry. Translation and energy differentiation generate these fields along periodic solutions, and two oscillatory fields generate them along the cylindrical solution. We also exhibit a first-order obstruction to improving these asymptotics by boundary-preserving conformal deformations of the flat models.

papers.title: An upper bound on the growth of minimal graphs
papers.abstract: Graphs of solutions to the minimal surface equation over simply connected domains with boundary values 0 can have at most exponential growth.

papers.title: The $L^p$ spectrum of the Stokes operator on hyperbolic 3-space and exponential decay for the Navier-Stokes equations
papers.abstract: We determine the $L^p$ spectrum, $1<p<\infty$, of the Stokes operator $A=-\PP\LD$ on divergence-free vector fields of hyperbolic 3-space of curvature $-a^2$, where $\LD=\Delta_B+\Ric$ is the Ebin-Marsden deformation Laplacian and $\PP$ is the Leray projector. The spectrum is the parabolic region $a^2\{4+z^2:\ z\in\C,\ |\im z|\le|1-2/p|\}$. For $p>2$ every interior point is an eigenvalue, realized by an explicit family of divergence-free swirl fields which leave $L^p$ exactly at the boundary of the region. It follows that the Stokes semigroup on $\Lp$ has exponential type exactly $-\mu_p$ with $\mu_p=a^2\bigl(4-(1-2/p)^2\bigr)$. At $p=3$ this is $35a^2/9$, which lies strictly above the rates $26a^2/9$ and $10a^2/3$ that follow from pointwise domination by the scalar heat semigroup and from interpolation, and strictly below the $L^2$ gap $4a^2$. For the Navier-Stokes equations with small data in $L^3$, whose global solvability on $\HH^3$ is due to Pierfelice, the solutions decay in $L^3$ and in $L^6$ at every rate below $\mu\cdot35a^2/9$, where $\mu$ is the viscosity, and no faster rate holds for the linearized flow. The exponent $3$ is the usual scaling threshold. Curvature fixes the time scale of the decay and introduces no new threshold.

papers.title: A Hadamard Formula for Equilibrium Envelopes under Parallel Deformation
papers.abstract: Let $(X,\omega_0)$ be a compact K\"ahler manifold of complex dimension $n$, and let $U\Subset X$ have $C^{3,1}$ uniformly strongly pseudoconvex boundary. Consider the signed parallel family $U_t=\{\rho<t\}$, where $\rho$ is a defining function agreeing near $\partial U$ with the signed distance, negative in $U$. Let $u_t$ be the equilibrium envelope with zero obstacle on $X\setminus U_t$, and write $\Sigma_t=\partial U_t$, with outward unit normal $\nu_t$. We prove that the normalized Monge--Amp\`ere energy $e(t)=E_{\omega_0}(u_t)$ belongs to $C^{1,1/2}([-\tau,\tau])$ for some $\tau>0$ and satisfies the Hadamard formula $$ e'(t)=\frac{1}{n+1}\int_{\Sigma_t}\left(-\partial_{\nu_t}u_t\right)^2 d\sigma_{\rho,t}^{\mathrm{tot}}, |t|<\tau. $$ Here $d\sigma_{\rho,t}^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the interior outward Anzellotti trace of $$ \frac{1}{V} d^c\rho\wedge \sum_{p=0}^{n-1}(p+1) \omega_{u_t}^{p}\wedge\omega_0^{n-1-p}, V=\int_X\omega_0^n, \omega_{u_t}=\omega_0+dd^c u_t. $$ This measure is positive and uniformly comparable to the induced surface measure. The proof combines uniform $C^{1,1}$ estimates up to the boundary from the interior with $1/2$-H\"older stability of the normal derivatives under the normal-flow identifications. We identify the boundary part of the normalized Monge--Amp\`ere measure with the negative outward trace of a divergence-measure flux current. The one-sided weak-* limits of the mixed Bedford--Taylor boundary measures yield the weighted total flux appearing in the variation formula.

papers.title: Critical-point-free energy for fractional-Toledo representations
papers.abstract: Let $S_g$ be a closed oriented surface of genus $g\ge2$. For a reductive representation $\rho:\pi_1(S_g)\to\mathrm{PU}(2,1)$, let $E_\rho$ be the energy function on Teichm\"uller space associated to equivariant harmonic maps into $\mathrm{CH}^2$. For every positive integer $d$ with $3\nmid d$, all sufficiently large $h$, and every $g>h$, we construct an irreducible reductive representation \[ \rho_{g,h,d}:\pi_1(S_g)\to\mathrm{PU}(2,1) \] with \[ \tau(\rho_{g,h,d})=2h-2-\frac{2d}{3}\notin\mathbb Z, \qquad \mathrm{Crit}(E_{\rho_{g,h,d}})=\varnothing. \] Consequently, the associated branched-minimal-surface forgetful map is not surjective in these nonintegral Toledo components.

papers.title: Index and nullity of critical spherical catenoids in hyperbolic three-space
papers.abstract: We prove that every critical spherical catenoid in a geodesic ball of hyperbolic three-space has Morse index four and nullity two. This resolves Medvedev's index conjecture throughout the parameter range of the catenoid family. The kernel consists precisely of the normal components of rotations that preserve the center of the ball and tilt the axis of the catenoid. As consequences, the radius of the supporting ball increases strictly along the family, and each critical spherical catenoid admits a smooth family of free boundary constant mean curvature deformations in its supporting ball. The proof combines a global boundary inequality obtained from a Wronskian, a positive Dirichlet eigenfunction supplied by the time component of the unit normal, and a Riccati comparison for the angular mode $k=2$. A ground-state identity then yields positivity of every angular mode $k\ge2$. We also show that the energy index of every critical spherical catenoid in $\mathbb{H^3}$, that is, the index of the second variation of its energy, equals four; hence the inequality between the energy index and the spectral index conjectured by Medvedev for geodesic balls of $\mathbb{H^n}$ fails.

papers.title: Local Aronson-B\'enilan estimates for the porous medium and fast diffusion equations on collapsing manifolds
papers.abstract: We establish local Aronson-B\'enilan estimates for positive solutions to the porous medium and fast diffusion equations on complete noncompact Riemannian manifolds with a small scale-invariant integral bound on the negative part of the Ricci curvature in $L^p$, where $p>n/2$. No uniform lower bound on the volume of unit balls is assumed, and hence the results apply to manifolds that may collapse. For the fast diffusion equation, we obtain the estimate in the range $1-2/n<m<1$. The auxiliary function method, which was designed for the heat equation under integral curvature conditions, is not directly applicable to those two nonlinear equations. The pressure operator in both cases contains a solution-dependent coefficient, which produces a residual term involving $\partial_t J$ in the evolution inequality. Its treatment requires a positive lower bound for $J$, and moreover, control of $-\partial_t\log J$. We obtain these bounds by linearizing the auxiliary equation, applying Duhamel's formula, and combining local Dirichlet heat kernel estimates with a singular Volterra inequality. Additionally, in the fast diffusion case, the negativity of $v$ changes the sign structure of the evolution inequality, so a separate coercive estimate is required to close the argument. Local Aronson-B\'enilan estimates follow for both diffusion regimes and integrating them along space-time curves gives the corresponding Harnack inequalities.

papers.title: A Positively Curved Seven-Manifold Without Effective Smooth Circle Actions
papers.abstract: We construct a compact Riemannian manifold $M$ with strictly positive sectional curvature and prove that $M$ admits no effective smooth $S^{1}$-action, which yields to a counterexample of a longstanding conjecture attributed to Yau.
